examples.knowledge_point: Factoring an Expression Containing a Sum of Squares
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's factor $-z$ from the expression. We have

$$
-z^3-25z =-z(z^2+25).
$$

Let's now focus on factoring the expression $\left( z^2+25\right).$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using $\textrm{i}^2 = -1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}+25 & ={z}^{2}-(-25) \\  & ={z}^{2}-(25{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & ={z}^{2}-(5\text{i})^{2} \\  & =(z+5\text{i})(z-5\text{i}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
-z(z^2+25)=-z(z+5\textrm i)(z-5\textrm i).
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that the given expression is a sum of squares, since

$$
9{m}^{4}+4{n}^{10}={(3{m}^{2})}^{2}+{(2{n}^{5})}^{2}.
$$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}9{m}^{4}+4{n}^{10} & =9{m}^{4}-(-4{n}^{10}) \\  & =9{m}^{4}-(4{\text{i}}^{2}{n}^{10}) \\  & ={(3{m}^{2})}^{2}-{(2\text{i}{n}^{5})}^{2} \\  & =(3{m}^{2}+2\text{i}{n}^{5})(3{m}^{2}-2\text{i}{n}^{5})\end{aligned}
$$
